title: Stalk and fibre dictionaries for flat-pullback association
statement:
Let $h:Y\to Z$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism], with $Z$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Fix $y\in Y$ and set $z=h(y)$, $A=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, and $M=\mathcal G_z$ (stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]). Write $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_B$ for the maximal ideals. For a ring $T$ and $T$-module $P$, let $\operatorname{Ann}_T(v)=\{a\in T:av=0\}$ and let $\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$ denote exact element-annihilator associated primes [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. On schemes use associated points [def-trf-relative-assassin]. Let $j_z:Y_z\to Y$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre projection [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and let $y_z$ be its unique point above $y$. Put $I=\mathfrak m_A B$ and $C=B/I$. Then:

(1) The stalk map $\varphi:A\to B$ is a flat local homomorphism (the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_B$ is $\mathfrak m_A$), and $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

(2) There is a $B$-linear isomorphism $(h^*\mathcal G)_y\cong M\otimes_A B$ (pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], tensor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]), and
$$y\in\operatorname{Ass}_Y(h^*\mathcal G)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(M\otimes_A B).$$
Also $z\in\operatorname{Ass}_Z(\mathcal G)$ if and only if $\mathfrak m_A\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(M)$.

(3) The fibre stalk map induces a ring isomorphism $C\cong\mathcal O_{Y_z,y_z}$ carrying $\mathfrak m_B/I$ to its maximal ideal. For every $v\in C$, with the $B$-action through $B\to C$,
$$\operatorname{Ann}_B(v)=\mathfrak m_B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Ann}_C(v)=\mathfrak m_B/I.$$
Consequently
$$y_z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_z}(\mathcal O_{Y_z})\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(C).$$
No Noetherianity of $B$ or finite generation of $M$ is assumed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-flat-morphism], flatness of $h$ means precisely that $B$ is flat over $A$ via the stalk map $\varphi$. The stalk map is local because a scheme morphism is a morphism of locally ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Thus $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. Conversely, if $a\notin\mathfrak m_A$, it is a unit of the local ring $A$, so $\varphi(a)$ is a unit and is not in $\mathfrak m_B$. Hence $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$.

Choose an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $z$ from the Noetherian affine cover in [pqf-def-locnoeth], and put $R=\mathcal O_Z(U)$. Then $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), the germ map $R\to A$ is localization at the complement of the prime corresponding to $z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to this localization to conclude that $A$ is Noetherian. This completes (1).

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), localization assertion; Properties Tag 01OV (definition-noetherian); Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] to $h$, $\mathcal G$, and $y$. It gives the asserted $B$-linear isomorphism $(h^*\mathcal G)_y\cong M\otimes_A B$. By [def-trf-relative-assassin], membership of $y$ in $\operatorname{Ass}_Y(h^*\mathcal G)$ means that $\mathfrak m_B$ is an exact element-annihilator associated prime of this stalk. A $B$-linear isomorphism preserves the annihilator of each element, since it is injective and commutes with multiplication by every $b\in B$; using [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes] gives the first equivalence in (2). Apply the same definition of associated points to $z$ and $\mathcal G$, whose stalk is $M$, to obtain the second equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0098 (lemma-stalk-pullback-modules); Divisors Tag 02OJ (definition-associated) and Tag 05DB (lemma-bourbaki), first stalk paragraph of proof

proof.text: The fibre projection identifies the points of $Y_z$ with the points of $Y$ above $z$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre], so $y_z$ is well defined and unique. Apply [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] to $h$ and $y$: the fibre stalk map $B\to\mathcal O_{Y_z,y_z}$ has kernel $I=\mathfrak m_A B$ and induces the asserted isomorphism $C\cong\mathcal O_{Y_z,y_z}$. Step 1 gives $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. The ideal $\mathfrak m_B/I$ is maximal because its quotient is the field $B/\mathfrak m_B$. Every element of $C$ outside this ideal is the image of an element outside $\mathfrak m_B$, hence is a unit. Thus this is the unique maximal ideal of $C$, and the ring isomorphism carries it to the maximal ideal of the fibre stalk.

Let $q:B\to C$ be the quotient map. For each $v\in C$ and $b\in B$, $bv=0$ in the restricted $B$-module if and only if $q(b)v=0$ in $C$. Therefore $\operatorname{Ann}_B(v)=q^{-1}(\operatorname{Ann}_C(v))$. Surjectivity of $q$ gives $q(q^{-1}(J))=J$ for every ideal $J$ of $C$, and $q^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B/I)=\mathfrak m_B$. These equalities prove both directions of the annihilator equivalence in (3). By [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes], membership of the maximal ideal in each associated-prime set is precisely existence of an element with that annihilator. Under the ring isomorphism of step 4, the same equations preserve annihilators of elements of the fibre local ring. Finally [def-trf-relative-assassin] identifies existence of an element with maximal annihilator in that stalk with $y_z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_z}(\mathcal O_{Y_z})$. This gives the final equivalence, without finiteness assumptions on $M$ or Noetherianity of $B$.
